newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 12.

text.p: Kirton to set terms for staying in NZ First: Neil Kirton would stay in Parliament as a NZ First backbencher if his caucus colleagues agreed to back him as he campaigned for delivery of the coalition agreement's promises on health, sources said on Monday night. Page 1.
Minister calls for report on legality of scratch game: Internal Affairs Minister Jack Elder has called for a report on the legality of a new scratch-and-win game. Page 1.

Condoms 'not sole solution': Free condoms in schools could give the wrong message to younger students unless they were also getting the message that it was okay not to be sexually active, Health Minister Bill English said on Monday. Page 2.

Airport considers Australian stake: Auckland International Airport is "contemplating" whether it will try to buy a stake in any of the 15 Australian airports officially on sale from this week. Page 13.

Interest lifts Prudential result: International financial services group Prudential Corporation, new owner of NZI Life, has reported an interim operating profit of $35.3 million for its Australian and New Zealand business. Page 13.
Big jump in hospital admissions: Patient members at Christchurch Hospital's emergency department are up sharply -- but stress is down. Page 1.

Radio Otago to extend South Island network: Radio Otago will announce another purchase soon in line with its plan to set up a South Island network, the chairman, John Farry, told the company's annual meeting on Monday. Page 33.
Nappies, $120 'bribe' to mums: Money intended for home help says hospital: New mothers are being offered $120 and a week of free nappies to leave hospital within 24 hours of having a baby.
Sex debate 'lacks values': Strong values are needed in the sex education debate, says the Minister of Health, Bill English, in rejecting a proposal to put free condoms in schools.

Maine's bankers ride to supplier's rescue: Suppliers to the beleaguered Levene and Palmer's Gardenworld stores finally got the good news they had been waiting for on Monday -- a NZ$40 million rescue package has been approved by Maine Investments' senior bankers.
Carpenter to hold majority: Asian Properties chairman Hotton Carpenter will be left holding about two-thirds of the company and have just nine other partners once the company is delisted.
